newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey to collect nuclear plant bids by Nov 25.
newsitem.headline: Turkey to collect nuclear plant bids by Nov 25.

text.p: Turkey, in need of urgent energy resources, will collect bids for its first nuclear power plant by November 25 for preliminary assessment, Energy Minister Recai Kutan told state Anatolian news agency on Friday.
"By November 25 we will have collected initial bids and later determine who will qualify for the actual tender," he said.
"We will later give qualifiers three months from February to make their actual bids. The result of the tender will be known in June," he said.

The nuclear power plant, to be built near the southern coastal village of Akkuyu near Mersin town, will be built either as single unit with a capacity of 1,200 MegaWatts (MW) or two equal units each having a capacity of 600 MW, he said.
He said the cost of the plant would be about $1.5 billion.
Some U.S. and Canadian firms had shown interest and were expected to give bids for the plant, to financed entirely by the builder, he said.

Industry analysts said firms interested in the project included France's Framatome, U.S. ABB Combustion Engineering, Westinghouse, Britain's General Electric Co Plc (GEC), Japan's Hitachi and Mitsubishi Corporation, a consortium between Canada's AECL and Britain's Kvaerner John Brown, Germany's Siemens and some local bidders.
